title: Add CI smoke tests for streaming stability + tool-call parsing + retry/backoff regressions
creator: Monica Patel
description:
We’ve seen repeated issues in early template testing and internal beta around: (1) SSE/streaming disconnects behind proxies, (2) tool-call parse/schema validation failures that surface as confusing exceptions, and (3) “helpful” changes to retry/backoff/timeouts that accidentally make streaming worse or cause request storms.

Add a small set of deterministic CI smoke tests that run on every PR to redwood-quickstarts (and optionally on a nightly schedule) to catch the top regressions early.

Scope is intentionally smoke-test level (not full eval harness). Tests should be fast (<5–7 minutes total), resilient to flakiness, and focused on “did we break the happy path + common failure modes?”

Key scenarios to cover:
- Streaming basic: start streaming, receive N chunks, graceful completion; validate we don’t stall and that we handle chunk boundaries.
- Streaming interruption: simulate mid-stream connection drop and confirm reconnect strategy does not duplicate tokens beyond an acceptable threshold; confirm error is typed and surfaced with troubleshooting hint.
- Tool-call parsing: model returns tool call; template validates schema; tool executes; tool result returned to model; final assistant response returned. Include at least one invalid tool payload test verifying we log and fail with a friendly error.
- Retry/backoff sanity: for transient 5xx/timeout, confirm we retry with exponential backoff + jitter; for 401/403/4xx (non-429) confirm we do NOT retry; for 429 confirm we backoff and respect Retry-After if present.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI job runs in GitHub Actions on PRs, no secrets required (uses mocked server) OR uses minimal token with safe limits + opt-in in repo settings.
- Tests have clear failure output (actionable message + link to troubleshooting section in README/docs).
- Flake mitigation: timeouts tuned, per-test retries limited, isolation between tests, and deterministic fixtures.
- Documented in /CONTRIBUTING.md (or repo testing docs) how to run locally.

Notes / constraints:
- Prefer a local mock gateway for determinism. Real API calls are acceptable only for a nightly “integration smoke” and must not block PR merges.
- Avoid high-cardinality telemetry fields in tests; logs should redact keys and never print full prompts/responses in CI output.

Links:
- Related work: PR #103 (retry/timeout defaults), PR #104 (tool-calling agent loop), PR #112 (CI smoke tests draft)
- Support signals: SUP-29410 (streaming disconnects), SUP-29441 (tool schema parse error), SUP-29435 (429 defaults)
- Threads: #devex streaming defaults alignment; CI flakiness discussion in #eng
comments: 2025-02-13 (Sabrina James): Drafted test plan. Proposal: run a mock SSE server + mock Redwood API to avoid dependency on real keys. For streaming reconnect behavior, simulate ECONNRESET after ~1–2 chunks and assert our wrapper produces either (a) a single terminal error type with request_id if available, or (b) successfully resumes with a new request_id captured. Need to align expectations with SDK behavior (TS vs Python differ).

2025-02-14 (Ibrahim Khan): +1 on mocked server for PR gating. If you need to validate SDK retry policy, do it via controlled responses (sequence: 503 -> 503 -> 200). Make sure we don’t accidentally retry streaming requests endlessly. For 429, respect Retry-After header when present; otherwise use capped exponential backoff.

2025-02-18 (Sahana Iyer): CI constraints: keep runtime <10 minutes; avoid docker-in-docker if possible. If you need a server, use a lightweight node/python process started in the workflow step. Add per-test timeout hard caps to avoid hanging runners.

2025-02-21 (Dana Lo): For tool-call parsing, include a test where tool arguments are malformed JSON / wrong type. In TS template we’ve seen Zod validation errors bubble up raw; we should assert we wrap with TemplateError(tool_schema_validation_failed) (or equivalent) and log a single-line summary that points to troubleshooting.

2025-02-25 (Christine Wong): Please add guardrails to avoid creating noisy retry loops in CI: overall test suite should fail fast and not spam logs. Also add one test to ensure we do not retry 401/invalid key. That’s a frequent support pattern and we don’t want to mask it.

2025-02-28 (Sabrina James): Implemented PR-level smoke tests for Python + TS templates using local mock server. Added: (1) streaming happy path with chunk assertions + stall timeout, (2) tool-call round trip with valid args + invalid args, (3) retry policy test matrix for 503/429/401. Added focused snapshot of error messages (no raw content). Total runtime ~4m30s on GHA runners.

2025-03-03 (Sahana Iyer): Reviewed workflow. Two flakes observed: streaming stall timeout too aggressive on slower runners; recommend bumping 2s -> 5s and reducing chunk count. Also ensure tests bind to 127.0.0.1 and random port to avoid collisions.

2025-03-04 (Sabrina James): Adjusted timeouts and chunk count; added randomized port binding and improved teardown. Added a per-test “attempts=2” at the harness level ONLY for the streaming interruption test, with strict cap (to avoid hiding real regressions).

2025-03-06 (Monica Patel): Approved + merged (PR #112). Follow-up: add optional nightly job against real Hosted API for end-to-end verification once telemetry header opt-in is finalized; should not gate PR merges.
